summary: Cecil Y. Lang studied at Duke University (~1937–1941) before holding posts at Yale University (~1949–1959), the University of Chicago (~1965–1970), and the University of Virginia (~1970–1991), where he served as Professor of English.

Cezary Galewicz is an Indologist associated with Jagiellonian University, where he held posts attested in 1996–1999, served as Adjunct Professor (attested 2012), and became Professor of Indian Civilisation in 2015.

Ch'ing-mao Cheng worked in Sinology and Japanology, earning degrees at National Taiwan University and Princeton. He taught at UC Berkeley (~1969–1976), chaired Asian Languages and Literatures at UMass Amherst (~1976–1996), and founded National Dong Hwa University, serving as Founding Chair (~1996–2003).

Chack-fan Lee, working in Buddhist studies and other fields, studied at the University of Hong Kong (~1964–1968) and the University of Western Ontario (~1969–1972). He served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor at the University of Hong Kong from 1994 to 2015.

Jae-sung Kim specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo under Yasunori Ejima (attested 1995) and held a post there (attested 1998–1999).

Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous traditional teachers, including Delog Dawa Drolma, Dudjom Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche, Khenpo Dorje, Jangchub Dorje, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Linguist Chaim Rabin studied at Hebrew University, SOAS, and Oxford (M.A., D.Phil.). He lectured at SOAS (1938–1941) and Oxford (1943–1956) before serving as Associate Professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1956–1985).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Chaisit Suwanvarangkul has held researcher positions at Kyoto University and the University of Delhi, and served as Lecturer in Buddhist Studies at the University of Otago (attested 2015).

Specializing in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology, Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad earned a doctorate at Oxford. After fellowships at Cambridge and Oxford and teaching at NUS, he became Professor (attested 2000–2012) and Distinguished Professor (attested 2026) at Lancaster University.

Chamnong Adivadhanasit, working in religious and Buddhist studies, earned a BA at Chulalongkorn University. In 2012, he was attested as Professor of Social Science at Kasetsart University and part-time instructor at Chulalongkorn University.
Champa Thupten Zongtse specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Göttingen, attested in 1991 and as a Lecturer in 2009.

Chandima Bogahawatta studied at University of Sri Jayewardenepura, PGIAR, and Shandong University (PhD). He served as Senior Lecturer at University of Kelaniya (2013) and Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Chandima Gangodawila earned a Ph.D. from the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (2010–2015). He was a research fellow at Victoria (2016–2017) and an assistant professor at Ateneo de Manila University (2025).
Historian Chandra R. de Silva served as Professor at the University of Peradeniya (attested 1991) and later as Dean of the College of Arts and Letters at Old Dominion University (attested 2006).

Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, Chandrabhal Tripathi earned his doctorate under Ernst Waldschmidt at Göttingen (~1957–1960). He held posts at Göttingen (~1962–1976) and Cologne, and served as Professor at Free University of Berlin (~1976–1994).

Chandrabhan P. Yadav earned a Ph.D. from Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2021. He served as Assistant Professor at Indraprastha College for Women (2020–2023) and joined the National Law School of India University as Assistant Professor in 2023.

Chandradhar Sharma Guleri, working in Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology, studied at the University of Allahabad (~1899–1903). He served as Head Pandit at Mayo College (~1904–1922) and held a post at Banaras Hindu University (~1920–1922).
Chandrika Das studied for a PhD in History at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University Delhi (2019–2026). She served as NCWEB Guest Faculty at the University of Delhi (2024–2025) and Miranda House (2025–2026).

Tibetologist Chang Huang studied at Wollongong, China University of Geosciences, and the University of Hong Kong (Ph.D. 2019–2023). He held postdoctoral posts at the University of Hong Kong (2024) and Wageningen University & Research (2024–2026).
Chang-geun Hwang completed a PhD in Buddhist studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000, where he studied under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Minoru Kiyota, and Morten Schlütter.
